_source: The game's own scripts, dumped to questmod-research/vanilla_scripts.reds, plus codexprobe2/ep1/journal/cooked_journal.journal serialized with WolvenKit.CLI. No DLL was read.
_why: OI-18 recorded two icon defects. One of them is not a defect, and the other is not where it was being looked for. Both conclusions come from reading the code that draws the widgets, so they are quoted here rather than remembered.

quest_list_icon._what: The icon beside a quest in the journal's left-hand list.
quest_list_icon._not: It is NOT a field on gameJournalQuest, and NOT districtID. gameJournalQuest has exactly four fields - title, type, recommendedLevelID, districtID - and no icon among them.
quest_list_icon._the_trap: gameJournalQuestType has TEN members. GetDisplayedCategory names nine. VehicleQuest (=6) is not among them, so it falls through to QuestListItemType.Invalid, and GetIcon's own fallthrough then returns the atlas part n"invalid" - the generic broken-icon glyph. A quest typed VehicleQuest is schema-valid, serializes cleanly, passes every build check and renders (!) with nothing reported anywhere. Vanilla itself ships one ep1 quest typed VehicleQuest.
quest_list_icon._ash_cache: type = SideQuest -> QuestListItemType.SideQuest -> atlas part 'minor_quest'. Valid; this is not the (!) path.

hud_quest_icon._what: A DIFFERENT icon - the one on the tracked-quest widget drawn by QuestItemController, not the journal list.
_chain: QuestItemController.SetQuestData (:371818, last line):  InkImageUtils.RequestSetImage(this, m_QuestIcon, "UIIcon." + ToString(m_QuestData.GetDistrict()))
m_district comes from JournalManager.GetDistrict(quest) (native), fed from gameJournalQuest.districtID
hud_quest_icon._shape: districtID is a CString holding a TweakDB path, 'Districts.<Name>'. Verified across all 55 gameJournalQuest entries of the ep1 journal: 39 set it (Districts.Dogtown, Districts.Pacifica, Districts.Heywood, Districts.SouthBadlands), 16 leave it empty.
hud_quest_icon._the_trap: The TweakDBID is built by STRING CONCATENATION from the gamedataDistrict enum name, so the icon record must be named UIIcon.<enum name> and not every district has one. gamedataDistrict has Dogtown_Brooklyn (56) and Dogtown_Worldmap_Sub (61); TweakDB has no UIIcon.Dogtown_Brooklyn and no UIIcon.Dogtown_Worldmap_Sub. A subdistrict that exists as a District record and as an enum member can still have no icon.
hud_quest_icon._ash_cache: districtID = Districts.Dogtown -> gamedataDistrict.Dogtown -> UIIcon.Dogtown, which exists. Valid.

codex_link_thumbnails._what: The linked-entry row on the journal screen. OI-18 called these 'three generic codex cards'.
codex_link_thumbnails._verdict: NOT A DEFECT. There is no generic card to fall back to.
codex_link_thumbnails._why_that_settles_it: An invalid link image HIDES the card. Three cards visible therefore means three valid link images, drawing their real art. IsImageValid is stricter still: it rejects a valid TweakDBID whose UIIcon resolves to atlas part 'empty', 'empty2' or 'c_empty' (:197429), so even a present-but-blank icon hides the card rather than drawing a placeholder.
codex_link_thumbnails._field: gameJournalQuestCodexLink carries ONE field, 'path'. The art is entirely the target gameJournalCodexEntry's business, via its linkImageId (the row thumbnail) or imageId (the full entry image).
codex_link_thumbnails._the_real_difference: Vanilla's row looks different because vanilla links CHARACTER codex entries alongside locations, and this mod links three locations. That is a content choice, not a pipeline fault. Adding a character portrait means linking a vanilla character's codex entry, or authoring a codex entry with its own linkImageId.

_untested: None of this has been seen in game since it was read. The claims are about which code path runs, and they are quoted from that code; whether the result looks right is still OI-18's to answer.
